title: 🌍 UNIT 7: CONTEMPORARY GLOBAL GEOGRAPHIC ISSUES AND PUBLIC CONCERNS
notes: Major contemporary geographic concerns include climate change, desertification, drought and famine.

title: 🌡️ 7.1 CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate change → long-term changes in the average state and variability of climate.

It has become a major global concern because it affects:
🔹 Human health
🔹 Agriculture and food production
🔹 Water resources
🔹 Ecosystems and biodiversity
🔹 Infrastructure and economies

⭐ Human activities, especially greenhouse-gas emissions, are a major driver of recent climate change.

title: 🔥 7.1.1 WHY CLIMATE CHANGE IS A GLOBAL CONCERN
notes:
Climate change has worldwide consequences because changes in temperature and precipitation affect natural and human systems.

Major concerns →
🧊 Melting glaciers and ice sheets
🌊 Sea-level rise
🌾 Changes in agricultural production
💧 Water stress and shortages
🔥 Increased drought and wildfire risks
🦋 Changes in species distribution
🏥 Increased health risks

⭐ Its impacts cross national boundaries, making international cooperation necessary.

title: 🏭 7.1.2 HUMAN-INDUCED CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
The major human cause of recent climate change is the increase of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, especially from fossil-fuel use.

Major sources →
🔹 Burning coal, oil and natural gas.
🔹 Land-use change and deforestation.
🔹 Agriculture and other human activities.

Important greenhouse gases → CO₂ + CH₄ + N₂O and other heat-trapping gases.

⭐ More greenhouse gases → stronger heat trapping → rising global temperatures.

title: 🌋 7.1.3 NATURAL CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Climate can also change naturally through changes in:

☀️ Incoming solar radiation
🌬️ Atmospheric composition
🌍 Earth's surface
🌊 Ocean-atmosphere circulation

Examples of natural influences → changes in solar output, volcanic activity and long-term variations in Earth's climate system.

⭐ Natural factors affect climate, but recent warming is dominated by human influence.

title: 🌾 7.1.4 EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
notes:
Major effects include:

🧊 Ice and glacier melting.
🌊 Sea-level rise.
🌡️ Increasing temperatures.
🌧️ Changes in rainfall patterns.
🔥 More severe drought and wildfire risks in some regions.
🌾 Reduced agricultural productivity in vulnerable areas.
💧 Increasing water stress.
🦋 Changes in species distribution and habitats.
🏥 Increased risks to human health.

⭐ Climate change affects both physical and socioeconomic systems.

title: 🌱 7.1.5 CLIMATE CHANGE & ETHIOPIA
notes:
Climate variability and change can affect Ethiopia through:

🌾 Agricultural production → changes in rainfall and temperature.

💧 Water resources → increased pressure during dry periods.

🐄 Livestock → reduced pasture and water availability during drought.

🌳 Ecosystems → stress on vegetation and natural resources.

🏠 Livelihoods → greater vulnerability of rain-fed and rural communities.

⭐ Adaptation is particularly important for climate-sensitive livelihoods.

title: 🛡️ 7.1.6 CLIMATE CHANGE RESPONSE
notes:
Two fundamental response strategies:

🛡️ Adaptation → adjusting ecological, social or economic systems to actual or expected climate impacts.

🔥 Mitigation → reducing greenhouse-gas emissions or increasing sinks that absorb and store them.

Examples:
🔹 Adaptation → irrigation, water harvesting, terracing, changing planting dates, crop diversification and tree planting.

🔹 Mitigation → renewable energy, energy efficiency, reduced fossil-fuel use and forest protection.

⭐ Adaptation manages impacts; mitigation addresses the causes.

title: 🔄 7.1.7 TYPES OF ADAPTATION
notes:
Adaptation can be classified as:

🔹 Reactive → occurs after climate impacts appear.

🔹 Anticipatory → occurs before impacts become apparent.

🔹 Private → carried out by households or companies.

🔹 Public → carried out in the public interest, often by government.

🔹 Planned → deliberate action based on policy or planning.

🔹 Autonomous → occurs naturally or independently in response to changing conditions.

title: 🏜️ 7.2 DESERTIFICATION
notes:
Desertification → land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas, caused by interacting human activities and climatic factors.

⚠️ Desertification is NOT simply the natural expansion of a desert into productive land.

⭐ It is a process of degradation occurring mainly in vulnerable drylands.

title: 🌵 7.2.1 DRYLANDS
notes:
Drylands include:

🏜️ Arid areas
🌾 Semi-arid areas
🌱 Dry sub-humid areas

Common characteristics →
🔹 Low and irregular precipitation.
🔹 Large temperature variations.
🔹 Poor organic matter in soils.
🔹 Limited water availability.
🔹 Vegetation and animals adapted to water scarcity.

⭐ Drylands are highly sensitive to environmental degradation.

title: 🌍 7.2.2 CAUSES OF DESERTIFICATION
notes:
Major causes include:

👥 Population growth → increases pressure on land and resources.

🌾 Over-cultivation → exhausts soil nutrients.

🐄 Overgrazing → removes protective vegetation.

🌳 Deforestation → destroys vegetation cover and increases erosion.

🔥 Bush and forest fires → damage vegetation.

💧 Poor irrigation → can contribute to land degradation.

🏗️ Large-scale projects → may disturb vulnerable environments.

🌡️ Climate change → can intensify environmental stress.

⭐ Human pressure + environmental stress → greater risk of desertification.

title: 📉 7.2.3 CONSEQUENCES OF DESERTIFICATION
notes:
Desertification can cause:

🔻 Soil erosion and declining fertility.
🌾 Lower crop yields.
💧 Poorer water quality.
🌳 Vegetation and habitat loss.
🦋 Biodiversity loss.
🍚 Food shortages and hunger.
💰 Poverty and economic losses.
🏃 Population migration.
⚔️ Conflict over land and freshwater.
🌊 Sedimentation and flooding problems.

⭐ Desertification can contribute to drought, food insecurity and famine, especially where poverty and conflict already exist.

title: 🇪🇦 7.2.4 DESERTIFICATION IN EASTERN AFRICA
notes:
Eastern Africa is highly vulnerable because large areas are dryland and many people depend directly on land resources.

Major pressures →
🔹 Rapid population growth.
🔹 Deforestation.
🔹 Overuse of land and vegetation.
🔹 Expansion of cultivation and grazing.
🔹 Large-scale environmental disturbance.
🔹 Poverty and limited alternative livelihoods.

🇪🇹 Ethiopia → desertification is particularly associated with vulnerable northern, northeastern and southeastern areas, with environmental pressure aggravated in some marginal areas by instability and conflict.

title: 🌳 7.2.5 COMBATING DESERTIFICATION
notes:
Important measures include:

🌱 Afforestation and tree planting.
⛰️ Soil and water conservation.
🌾 Improved agricultural practices.
🐄 Better grazing management.
🌳 Protection of natural vegetation.
💧 Efficient water management.
👨‍🌾 Agricultural extension and community participation.

🇪🇹 Ethiopian example → Green Legacy and tree-planting efforts contribute to environmental restoration.

⭐ Prevention is more effective when land users participate in conservation.

title: 💧 7.3 DROUGHT
notes:
Drought → a temporary and significant reduction in water or moisture availability below the normal or expected level for a specified period.

⭐ Key features → temporary + significant + below normal + specified period.

Drought differs from aridity:
🔹 Aridity → long-term climatic dryness.
🔹 Drought → temporary shortage relative to normal conditions.

title: 🌍 7.3.1 DROUGHT-PRONE REGIONS
notes:
Major dryland belts include:

1️⃣ Sonoran Desert and southwestern United States.
2️⃣ Atacama region along the Andes.
3️⃣ The broad dry belt from the Atlantic toward China, including the Sahara and Arabian deserts.
4️⃣ Namib-Kalahari region of Southern Africa.
5️⃣ Most of Australia.

⭐ Within these broad belts are arid, dryland, semi-arid and dry-subhumid zones.

title: 📊 7.3.2 TYPES OF DROUGHT
notes:
1️⃣ Meteorological drought → deficiency of precipitation compared with normal conditions.

2️⃣ Hydrological drought → shortage of water in rivers, lakes, reservoirs and groundwater.

3️⃣ Agricultural drought → insufficient soil moisture for crops and agricultural production.

⭐ Meteorological → rainfall | Hydrological → water resources | Agricultural → crops and soil moisture.

title: 📐 7.3.3 DROUGHT INDICES
notes:
Drought indices help measure the severity and characteristics of drought.

Common indices →
🔹 Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI)
🔹 Crop Moisture Index (CMI)
🔹 Satellite Vegetation Health Index
🔹 Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI)

⭐ SPI → based on long-term precipitation records; negative values indicate dry conditions.

title: 🌦️ 7.3.4 CAUSES OF DROUGHT
notes:
Natural factors →
🔹 El Niño
🔹 La Niña
🔹 Ocean warming
🔹 Shifts in the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
🔹 Changing rainfall patterns

Human-related factors →
🔹 Land-cover change
🔹 Land-use change
🔹 Greenhouse-gas emissions
🔹 Environmental degradation

⭐ Drought results from interacting climatic and human-environment factors.

title: 🌾 7.3.5 DROUGHT & AGRICULTURE
notes:
The effect of drought on crops depends on:

💧 Proportion of irrigated production.
🌱 Soil moisture-retention capacity.
🌧️ Timing of rainfall during the growing season.
👨‍🌾 Farmers' adaptive behavior.
📏 How drought is defined and measured.

⭐ Low rainfall does not produce identical agricultural impacts everywhere.

title: 📉 7.3.6 EFFECTS OF DROUGHT
notes:
Major effects include:

🌾 Crop failure and reduced food production.
🐄 Livestock losses.
💧 Water shortages.
💰 Reduced household income and economic activity.
🍚 Food insecurity.
🏃 Migration.
⚔️ Competition over scarce water resources.
🏫 Reduced school attendance in affected communities.

⭐ Drought can create severe social and economic consequences beyond agriculture.

title: 🌾 7.3.7 DROUGHT MANAGEMENT
notes:
Important measures include:

🔹 Irrigation and efficient water use.
🔹 Water harvesting and storage.
🔹 Drought-resistant crops.
🔹 Crop diversification.
🔹 Soil and water conservation.
🔹 Early-warning systems.
🔹 Improved drought monitoring.
🔹 Livelihood diversification.
🔹 Preparedness and emergency assistance.

⭐ Early warning + preparedness + adaptation → reduce drought impacts.

title: 🍚 7.4 FAMINE
notes:
Famine → a process in which food availability or people's entitlement/access to food declines enough to cause widespread and substantially increased illness and death.

⭐ Famine is more than hunger; it involves a severe breakdown in food access and security affecting large populations.

title: 🔑 7.4.1 FOOD SECURITY & FAMINE
notes:
Food security → a condition in which people have reliable access to sufficient food.

Famine can develop when:
🔹 Food availability declines.
🔹 People's ability to acquire food decreases.
🔹 Distribution systems fail.
🔹 Livelihoods and purchasing power collapse.

⭐ Food production + distribution + access/entitlements are central to understanding famine.

title: 🌾 7.4.2 CAUSES OF FAMINE
notes:
Natural causes →
🔹 Agricultural drought
🔹 Floods
🔹 High winds
🔹 Frost or unusual cold
🔹 Crop diseases
🔹 Pest invasions such as locusts

Human causes →
🔹 Conflict and destruction of agricultural production.
🔹 Economic shocks.
🔹 Poor macroeconomic management.
🔹 Poor agricultural pricing policies.
🔹 Forced procurement of farm products.
🔹 Excessive food exports that reduce domestic availability.

⭐ Famine usually results from multiple interacting causes.

title: 💰 7.4.3 FOOD ACCESS & ENTITLEMENTS
notes:
Famine can occur even when food exists if people cannot obtain it.

Access can be reduced by:
🔹 Loss of income or employment.
🔹 High food prices.
🔹 Loss of livestock or crops.
🔹 Conflict and displacement.
🔹 Disruption of markets and transport.
🔹 Reduced purchasing power.

⭐ Food availability ≠ food access. People need both sufficient food supplies and the ability to obtain food.

title: 🇪🇹 7.4.4 FAMINE IN ETHIOPIA
notes:
Ethiopia has experienced severe famines at different periods.

⭐ The 1984–1985 famine is identified as the most disastrous famine in modern Ethiopian history.

Famine vulnerability can be increased by:
🔹 Drought
🔹 Crop failure
🔹 Poverty
🔹 Conflict
🔹 Weak food access
🔹 Livelihood dependence on rainfall

title: 🛡️ 7.4.5 MEASURES TO MAINTAIN FOOD SECURITY
notes:
Short-term measures should protect people's access to food by:

1️⃣ Ensuring food availability in affected areas.
2️⃣ Protecting the food entitlements of affected groups.

Major measures →
🔹 Price stabilization.
🔹 Food subsidies.
🔹 Employment-creation programs.
🔹 General food distribution.
🔹 Supplementary feeding.
🔹 Livestock and pastoralist support.
🔹 Water programs.
🔹 Health programs.

title: 🔗 7.5 RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CLIMATE CHANGE, DESERTIFICATION, DROUGHT & FAMINE
notes:
🌡️ Climate change → can alter rainfall and temperature patterns.

💧 Drought → prolonged shortage of rainfall/moisture.

🏜️ Land degradation + drought → can accelerate desertification in vulnerable drylands.

🌾 Drought/desertification → reduce agricultural productivity and livelihoods.

🍚 Reduced food production + reduced food access → can increase food insecurity and contribute to famine.

⚔️ Poverty and conflict → can intensify these effects.

⭐ The relationship is not always a simple one-way chain; natural and human factors interact.

title: 🧠 UNIT 7 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🌡️ Climate change → long-term changes in climate conditions.

🏜️ Desertification → land degradation in drylands.

💧 Drought → temporary significant reduction in water/moisture below normal.

🍚 Famine → severe food crisis causing widespread increased illness and death.

🛡️ Adaptation → adjust to climate impacts.

🔥 Mitigation → reduce greenhouse-gas emissions or increase sinks.

🌧️ Meteorological drought → rainfall shortage.

💧 Hydrological drought → water-resource shortage.

🌾 Agricultural drought → insufficient moisture for crops.

⭐ Food availability → amount of food present.

⭐ Food access/entitlement → people's ability to obtain food.

🌳 Main causes → population pressure + over-cultivation + overgrazing + deforestation + poor land use + climate stress.

💧 Drought → temporary significant moisture/water shortage below normal.

📊 Types → meteorological + hydrological + agricultural.

📐 Indices → PDSI + CMI + Satellite Vegetation Health Index + SPI.

🌦️ Causes → El Niño + La Niña + ocean warming + ITCZ shifts + land-cover change + greenhouse emissions.
